questions.label: Q1
questions.question: Does the claim state that the tenant is married or in a registered partnership and that the rented dwelling serves as the family home?

questions.label: Q2
questions.question: Does the tenant seek an extension of the lease because having to leave by the end date would be a hardship for the tenant or the tenant's family?

questions.label: Q3
questions.question: Does the notice or the claim state that the landlord terminated because the tenant did not pay overdue rent or accessory charges within a time limit the landlord had set?

questions.label: Q4
questions.question: Has the landlord given the tenant notice terminating the lease of the dwelling, and has it reached the tenant?

questions.label: Q5
questions.question: Does the claim state that the landlord gave notice because the tenant had, in good faith, asserted claims under the lease (for example demanded repair of a defect or contested the rent)?

text:
Dear advice team,

Let me start with what this is not about. We have never had a quarrel with Sonnbühl Services Ltd. We never asked them for repairs, never questioned the rent, never complained about anything. When I called Ms Alice Marti, she said quite openly that the owner wants the flat for his daughter. So I don't think anyone is punishing us for anything; it's simply that they want us out.

The termination letter came by registered post. I picked it up at the Emmen post office on Saturday, 16 May 2026, and opened it right there at the counter. It says we have to leave our flat at Schulhausstrasse 94 by the end of September.

That is just over four months, and for us it would be a disaster. Our daughter is two, and our second child is due at the end of August, so we would be moving with a newborn in the middle of all that. On top of this, rents around Emmen have shot up; we pay CHF 2380 now and everything comparable we've looked at is far above that. I'd like to ask for the lease to be extended, at least until spring, so we have a fair chance to find something and the baby isn't born into packing boxes.

I should add that I'm married to Megan Imhof. The flat at Schulhausstrasse 94 has been our family home since we moved in together in February 2023, and it's where we're raising our children.

Attached is the Swiss Post tracking printout showing when the letter reached me.

With thanks and kind regards,
Laura Moser
